title: A Unified SVD-Modal Solution for Sparse Sound Field Reconstruction with Hybrid Spherical-Linear Microphone Arrays
status: Official conference program verified; inspected text is arXiv v1; IEEE full text not accessed
readingDepth: Official program page; arXiv abstract and PDF sections 1–4, equations (1)–(13); PDF p.2 equations (4)–(7) visually inspected
claim: Uses hybrid-array measurement matrices and an SVD modal representation for sparse reconstruction; reported evaluation uses simulated reverberant rooms.
limits: No replication; sparse/model assumptions restrict recovery. Finite matrices do not certify full continuum observability.
notationIssue: Printed Eq. (6) defines y~=U_K* y and H~=Sigma_K^-1 V_K*. With Eq. (4), the projected dictionary should be Sigma_K V_K*, or both sides should be consistently whitened to Sigma_K^-1 U_K* y=V_K* x. Requires clarification before implementation. No claim about authors' code.

title: On an inverse boundary problem in elastodynamics
readingDepth: PDF pp.1–6: formulation, Theorems 1.1–1.3, Remarks 1.1–1.5, weak boundary form; proofs not audited
claim: Static inverse-elasticity uniqueness under specified structural or directional quasianalytic shear-modulus assumptions; a torsional channel can determine shear modulus while remaining independent of lambda.
limits: Partial data conclusions have exact domain, geometry and coefficient assumptions. Title notwithstanding, inspected results concern static elasticity. No implementation or experimental replication.

title: Permutation-Invariant Physics-Informed Neural Network for Region-to-Region Sound Field Reconstruction
status: Preprint; no conference status asserted in this review
readingDepth: Abstract, sections 1–3.2, acoustic transfer-function/Helmholtz/reciprocity definitions and equations (1)–(6)
claim: Builds reciprocal source/receiver exchange symmetry into a learned acoustic transfer-function representation and includes physics residuals.
limits: Symmetry by construction does not prove correct recovery, global PDE satisfaction from finite collocation, or applicability outside the linear reciprocal acoustic model. Training and benchmark results not reproduced.

title: Boundary-condition identification from a scale-invariant frequency ratio in shear-deformable and nonlocal beams and plates
readingDepth: Abstract, introduction, sections 5.5–5.6 and selected sections 6.1–6.5
claim: Studies two-mode spectral-ratio shifts as indicators of support changes in specified beam/plate models, with an explicitly nonunique tip-support regime.
limits: Known support family and model regime required; uniform scale cancellation does not remove thickness or slenderness sensitivity. Experimental realization is identified as future work in section 5.6. No replication.
